A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monetary accommodation in Yugoslavia was not a policy choice, but rather an unavoidable by-product of a soft-budget constraint regime.
monetary accommodation in transition economies can be a result of the presence of soft-budget constraints, and that the role of aggregate-supply shocks is crucial.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the monetary policy stance of the Yugoslav central bank was passive in accommodating wage inflation in the 1970's and 1980's, while being more active in the 1990's.
monetary policy can play a role in stabilizing the economy in transition, provided that it is not used to accommodate wage inflation.
